question: Is customer data encrypted at rest, and where are the keys kept?
gold_answer: Yes. Customer/workspace data is encrypted at rest with AES-256; keys are managed in AWS KMS and retained in the same AWS region as the protected data.
must_have_facts: Yes. Customer/workspace data is encrypted at rest with AES-256; keys are managed in AWS KMS and retained in the same AWS region as the protected data.
agent_answer: Yes. All Restricted and Confidential data at rest is encrypted with AES-256 or an equivalent-strength algorithm approved by Security Engineering. This covers production databases and read replicas, S3 object storage, block storage, backups and snapshots, and log storage. Encryption keys are managed in AWS Key Management Service (KMS) and kept separate by region: keys for EU customer data are created and stored in eu-west-1, and keys for US customer data in us-east-1. Keys rotate automatically every year, cannot be exported from KMS in plaintext, and only a small group in Security Engineering can administer them, with key use logged in AWS CloudTrail.
